turns.text: Did you know that alcohol prevents your body from going into a deep sleep?

dialogues.title: Going hiking
dialogues.intro: Jen and Teddy are making some plans for the weekend.

turns.speaker: Jen
turns.text: Ted, It's been a while. Do you want to do something this weekend?

turns.speaker: Teddy
turns.text: I know, right? We haven't hung out in months. I'd love to do something. What do you think we should do?

turns.speaker: Jen
turns.text: The weather is going to be nice on Sunday. What about a hike? And then we can get some dinner afterwards?

turns.speaker: Teddy
turns.text: That's great. Let's go to Golden Ears. I haven't been there in a long time.

turns.speaker: Jen
turns.text: Perfect. I can drive. I'll pick you up at 12:00?

turns.speaker: Teddy
turns.text: Okay. See you then! And since you're driving, I'll bring some snacks to share.

turns.speaker: Jen
turns.text: Great.

dialogues.title: Scattered Showers
dialogues.intro: Ted and Lindsay are talking about the weather.

turns.speaker: Ted
turns.text: What's the weather forecast looking like this weekend? We should get out for a hike.

turns.speaker: Lindsay
turns.text: Let me check. Clear skies on Saturday but scattered showers on Sunday. Hot and humid both days.

turns.speaker: Ted
turns.text: If were going to go to Mount Hood, we need to be prepared for anything. It can go from calm to gale-force winds so quickly.

turns.speaker: Lindsay
turns.text: That happened last time I was there. Just light rain at first and then the storm clouds rolled in and there were wind gusts of more than 100 km/h.

turns.speaker: Richard
turns.text: Did you hear about the fight between Tom and Carrie? Sparks were flying!

turns.speaker: Candice
turns.text: Oh yeah, it's out in the open now. I think it's common knowledge. I heard that Tom didn't want to play hardball and he was happy to let the client do things under the table with regard to their taxes.

turns.speaker: Richard
turns.text: Yeah, and Carrie disagreed and thought it was to either get them to do things the right way or bail on them.

turns.speaker: Candice
turns.text: No harm done. I think it's settled down now. I'm happy I don't make the decisions around here!

dialogues.title: From Dawn Till Dusk
dialogues.intro: Mandy is talking to Eric about how her work is going.

turns.speaker: Eric
turns.text: How's work going these days?

turns.speaker: Mandy
turns.text: Same old, same old. I have to work from dawn till dusk. We have all these strict deadlines from clients and are always running out of time.

turns.speaker: Eric
turns.text: Can you cut back on your hours? That's terrible not having any free time.

turns.speaker: Mandy
turns.text: Not if I want to get ahead in this industry. I'd love to take my time on projects and not be in a rush too. But, that's not going to cut it.

dialogues.title: Please give me a hand
dialogues.intro: Terry is asking Jay for some help with his son.

turns.speaker: Terry
turns.text: Could you please give me a hand this weekend?

turns.speaker: Jay
turns.text: Sure, what do you need? I have a bit of free time.

turns.speaker: Terry
turns.text: Would you mind looking after Todd during my dentist appointment?

turns.speaker: Jay
turns.text: Okay, no problem. I love hanging out with him. When and where?

turns.speaker: Terry
turns.text: It's on Saturday from 2-4. You can come over to my house? Or, I can drop him off at yours.

turns.speaker: Jay
turns.text: Bring him over to my house. We'll watch a movie.

dialogues.title: Surf the Web
dialogues.intro: Tom is talking about helping his grandma access the Internet.

turns.speaker: Terry
turns.text: Do you want to grab dinner after work?

turns.speaker: Tom
turns.text: Sorry, I can't. I have to help my 90-year old grandma access the Internet. She got the Internet hooked up but can't surf the web for some reason.

turns.speaker: Terry
turns.text: That's amazing. My mom barely knows how to get online or check her email and she's only 60.

turns.speaker: Tom
turns.text: I know, right? Plus she has all sorts of social media accounts like Facebook and Pinterest.

dialogues.title: For the Time Being
dialogues.intro: Sid and Ho-Hyun are talking about how busy they are (or arent).

turns.speaker: Sid
turns.text: What's up these days Ho-Hyun?

turns.speaker: Ho-Hyun
turns.text: Did you hear? I lost my job because of Covid last month. The restaurant I'm working at closed. I have a lot of time on my hands these days.

turns.speaker: Sid
turns.text: So what do you do?

turns.speaker: Ho-Hyun
turns.text: For the time being, I'm just enjoying myself. I rarely have time to do that as a chef. I pass the time of day with my neighbor, watch some Netflix and try to go for a walk every day. What are you up to?

turns.speaker: Sid
turns.text: At the moment, I'm also looking for work. I still have my old job but I don't really like it that much. I'm seeing what else is out there. Formerly, it was okay but my boss left and the new guy is terrible.

turns.speaker: Ho-Hyun
turns.text: Sorry to hear that.

dialogues.title: Burst Out
dialogues.intro: Zeke is telling his friend Ted about something that happened at work.

turns.speaker: Ted
turns.text: How was your day?

turns.speaker: Zeke
turns.text: Okay. So the craziest thing happened at work today! We were in a meeting and our boss called on Tommy to ask him his opinion about something. But, he was dozing off. He woke up and let out the biggest snort!

turns.speaker: Ted
turns.text: Come on. That didn't happen, did it? I don't believe you.

turns.speaker: Zeke
turns.text: For real. Why would I make it up? I almost fell out of my chair. I was laughing so hard. I don't think I can get over it. Every time I see Tommy now, I want to laugh.

turns.speaker: Ted
turns.text: What did your boss do?

turns.speaker: Zeke
turns.text: He was cool and just burst out laughing. We've all caught Tommy sleeping before but he's so good at his job that he can get away with it.

dialogues.title: Going to the Beach
dialogues.intro: Tanya and Shannon are talking about going to the beach the next day.

turns.speaker: Tanya
turns.text: Shannon, I checked the weather forecast. Highs of 28 tomorrow and sunny, Let's go to the beach.

turns.speaker: Shannon
turns.text: Really? Yeah, let's gol

turns.speaker: Tanya
turns.text: Should we go to Jericho Beach?

turns.speaker: Shannon
turns.text: Yeah, that's a nice place. There's not a lot of parking though. Should we go later at like 4:00 when all the families have left?

turns.speaker: Tanya
turns.text: Definitely. We can stay for the sunset.

turns.speaker: Shannon
turns.text: Rad. Why don't I pick you up around 3:30?

turns.speaker: Tanya
turns.text: Awesome. I'll see you then.

dialogues.title: Please turn up the music
dialogues.intro: Tim can't hear well and wants to turn up the music.

turns.speaker: Tim
turns.text: Do you mind if I turn up the music? I love this song.

turns.speaker: Jen
turns.text: No, go ahead. It's fine with me. It is a bit quiet for me too.

turns.speaker: Tim
turns.text: And is it a bit cold in here?

turns.speaker: Jen
turns.text: Okay. I'll turn up the heat. It'll take a while to warm up though. Do you want to borrow a sweater or a blanket?

turns.speaker: Tim
turns.text: I'd love a blanket. I don't know what's wrong with me. I'm always cold these days.

turns.speaker: Jen
turns.text: Are you feeling okay? Maybe something is going on? You're usually hot, right?

turns.speaker: Tim
turns.text: I don't know. I just had a check-up at the doctor and everything was fine.

dialogues.title: Catch My Eye
dialogues.intro: Jerry and Sid are talking about coming late to class.

turns.speaker: Jerry
turns.text: Hey Sid, can you save me a seat in class? I'm going to come late.

turns.speaker: Sid
turns.text: Take your time. Ill even take notes for you. But, why are you always late?

turns.speaker: Jerry
turns.text: You know the cute girls always catch my eye and then I have to stop and talk. But, keep up the good work my friend. I love that you always pay attention in class.

turns.speaker: Sid
turns.text: We should have lunch after class. What do you think?

turns.speaker: Jerry
turns.text: Sounds great. It's my treat.

dialogues.title: Opening Night
dialogues.intro: Sid and Manny are talking about the new James Bond movie.

turns.speaker: Sid
turns.text: Are you going to watch that new James Bond movie? It comes out on the 22%e

turns.speaker: Manny
turns.text: Oh yeah, I never miss an opening night for a Bond movie. I've seen the movie trailer at least 10 times now. It's going to be a huge box office hit.

turns.speaker: Sid
turns.text: I heard that Tom Cruise has a supporting role and that Brad Pitt plays the main character. That's pretty impressive.

turns.speaker: Manny
turns.text: For sure. What about you? Will you be there on opening night?

turns.speaker: Sid
turns.text: Not in the movie theater but I'll watch it when I can download it for free!

dialogues.title: Come Over
dialogues.intro: Ethan and Allan are talking about hanging out after work.

turns.speaker: Ethan
turns.text: Hey, do you want to come over after work today for a beer?

turns.speaker: Allan
turns.text: Sure I'll drop in on my way home. I would love to kick back. It's been a long week

turns.speaker: Ethan
turns.text: Well, let yourself in. I'll be on the patio around back. I might ring up Tony too and see if he can join us.

turns.speaker: Allan
turns.text: Sure Oh yeah. Ill stop by the bank and pick up some cash. I have to pay you back for last weekend.

turns.speaker: Ethan
turns.text: That's right. Okay. We'll figure it out.

dialogues.title: Where do you Live?
dialogues.intro: Toby and Casey are co-workers who are talking about where they live.

turns.speaker: Toby
turns.text: Traffic was so bad this morning!

turns.speaker: Casey
turns.text: Oh, I don't have a commute. just walk to work. Where do you live?

turns.speaker: Toby
turns.text: I live in Edgemont.

turns.speaker: Casey
turns.text: Wow, that's far! How long does it take you to get to work?

turns.speaker: Toby
turns.text: Well, optimistically, only 30 minutes. But, it's usually closer to an hour. Where do you live?

turns.speaker: Casey
turns.text: You know the high rise across the street? That's where I live.

turns.speaker: Toby
turns.text: Amazing. I'd go home for lunch if I was so close.

turns.speaker: Casey
turns.text: I often do. I guess people think I go out for lunch but I'm usually just hanging out at home.

dialogues.title: Getting to a Concert
dialogues.intro: Bob and Kevin are talking about how to get downtown for a concert.

turns.speaker: Kevin
turns.text: Where's the concert? And what time is it?

turns.speaker: Bob
turns.text: It's at The Orpheum, downtown. It starts at 9:00.

turns.speaker: Kevin
turns.text: Parking is so expensive around there. What about taking the Skytrain there instead of driving?

turns.speaker: Bob
turns.text: That's good for getting there, but it probably stops running around 11:00. We might have to take an Uber home.

turns.speaker: Kevin
turns.text: That's fine with me. It won't be too expensive if we split it.

dialogues.title: Every Winter
dialogues.intro: Katie and Kim are talking about the first snow of the year.

turns.speaker: Katie
turns.text: Did you hear that it's going to snow tomorrow evening?

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Really? That seems earlier than normal. I was hoping it wouldn't happen until next month.

turns.speaker: Katie
turns.text: I don't think so. Doesn't it always happen around Halloween every year?

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: You're right I guess. Every winter, I'm always happy on the first day of snow but then I hate it!

turns.speaker: Katie
turns.text: I don't mind. The kids love making snowmen and sledding. They spend more time outside when there's lots of snow.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: True, but I'm the one who has to shovel the driveway!

dialogues.title: Apply for University
dialogues.intro: John is talking to Ted about his plans for after high school.

turns.speaker: Ted
turns.text: Are you in your last year of high school?

turns.speaker: John
turns.text: Yes, I'll be finished in a few months from now.

turns.speaker: Ted
turns.text: Congratulations! Did you apply to university?

turns.speaker: John
turns.text: Yes, for the University of Toronto. I get good grades so I should get in. I even hope to get a scholarship.

turns.speaker: Ted
turns.text: That's great! Did you choose a major?

turns.speaker: John
turns.text: Not yet. Everyone does general studies in their first year. But next year, I want to choose something so I can have a good salary when I graduate.

turns.speaker: Ted
turns.text: Makes sense to me.

dialogues.title: Electricity Bill
dialogues.intro: Keith and Tanya are talking about what they can do to reduce electricity usage.

turns.speaker: Tanya
turns.text: I'm wondering if we can save money on our bills and save the environment at the same time?

turns.speaker: Keith
turns.text: I don't keep track of the electricity bill. Has it gone up?

turns.speaker: Tanya
turns.text: The rates have gone up, yes. I think we can save electricity in a few different ways.

turns.speaker: Keith
turns.text: Will it make a difference? Aren't things like replacing lightbulbs mostly a waste of time?

turns.speaker: Tanya
turns.text: We can save energy in several ways. I found this helpful guide online. We can try a few of the things in it.

turns.speaker: Keith
turns.text: Okay, let's do it.

dialogues.title: Out Walking the Dog
dialogues.intro: Trina sees her neighbor Bob when walking her dog.

turns.speaker: Trina
turns.text: Hey Bob! How are you?

turns.speaker: Bob
turns.text: Pretty good. I don't remember you having a dog. Did you just get him?

turns.speaker: Trina
turns.text: It's a girl. Yeah, we got Riley last week.

turns.speaker: Bob
turns.text: Nice. Where did you get her?

turns.speaker: Trina
turns.text: At the shelter. I let the kids pick her out. She was super friendly and it was an easy choice.

turns.speaker: Bob
turns.text: And how's it going at your house?

turns.speaker: Trina
turns.text: Well, Riley ruined our couch and has eaten a ton of shoes already but I don't care. She's so funny and cute. I love her so much already.

turns.speaker: Bob
turns.text: Sounds like exciting times at your place.

dialogues.title: Dry Out
dialogues.intro: Keith and Ken are talking about cleaning up after their camping trip.

turns.speaker: Keith
turns.text: Ugggh...I hate packing up camp in the rain! But, we're almost home so let's think ahead about how were going to unpack.

turns.speaker: Ken
turns.text: Good idea. Well, we need to dry out the tent so let's work together to hang it up. Oh, and let's plug in our phones first. They're both dead I think, right?

turns.speaker: Keith
turns.text: I can take in all the food and wipe out the cooler after that.

turns.speaker: Ken
turns.text: Sure. And If look up the number for that pizza place we like! I'm so hungry for real food. I can order something and by the time it arrives, we'll hopefully be done unpacking.

dialogues.title: Asking for Money
dialogues.intro: Steve is asking his Dad for some money.

turns.speaker: Steve
turns.text: Dad, I need twenty bucks.

turns.speaker: Dad
turns.text: Didn't I just give you your allowance? What happened to that?

turns.speaker: Steve
turns.text: My friends and I went out for lunch yesterday at school. It's all gone.

turns.speaker: Dad
turns.text: So what do you need the cash for?

turns.speaker: Steve
turns.text: Everyone is going out for lunch today too.

turns.speaker: Dad
turns.text: You can bring lunch from home and it's freel Seriously. Just take anything you want out of the fridge. No charge.

turns.speaker: Steve
turns.text: So will you give me the money?

turns.speaker: Dad
turns.text: No. I don't eat out as much as you do and I'm the one who makes all the money!

turns.speaker: Steve
turns.text: Daaaaaaadddd! It's so unfair.

turns.speaker: Dad
turns.text: Have you thought about getting a part-time job?

dialogues.title: Home-Cooked Meals
dialogues.intro: Sun and Todd are talking about eating habits.

turns.speaker: Sun
turns.text: Do you have a New Year's resolution for 2021?

turns.speaker: Todd
turns.text: A big one! I want to change my eating habits by not eating so much junk food and processed food. I'm going to focus on home-cooked meals and smaller portion sizes.

turns.speaker: Sun
turns.text: Mine is very similar. Im not going to go on a diet but / want to eat a balanced diet with more fruits and vegetables. And I want to avoid the second helpings, especially at dinner.

turns.speaker: Todd
turns.text: I hope we can do it.

dialogues.title: Talking about chores
dialogues.intro: Tony and Emma are talking about a plan for cleaning their house.

turns.speaker: Tony
turns.text: Our house is so messy and dirty. I hate it.

turns.speaker: Emma
turns.text: I know. I'm thinking the same thing. Let's clean up. Why don't we put all the stuff away first? Then it'll be easier to clean.

turns.speaker: Tony
turns.text: Good plan. After that, I'll tackle the bathrooms and you can do the floors. Sound fair?

turns.speaker: Emma
turns.text: Sure. I'll throw a load of laundry in first and work on that while I do the floors.

turns.speaker: Tony
turns.text: Okay. Then we can dust and clean up the kitchen and whatever else there is to do.

turns.speaker: Emma
turns.text: Uggghhh... this is going to take us hours! Why are we so dirty?

dialogues.title: Go to the Doctor
dialogues.intro: Anita is talking to Ted about how sick she has been.

turns.speaker: Ted
turns.text: Hey Anita, what's up?

turns.speaker: Anita
turns.text: I've had a rough couple of weeks. I caught a cold and it took me a while to recover. I was just getting ready for Christmas too. It was terrible timing.

turns.speaker: Ted
turns.text: Oh no! Did you go to the doctor?

turns.speaker: Anita
turns.text: Yes, she said to take some over-the-counter medications because it was a virus.

turns.speaker: Ted
turns.text: Well, that's better than taking antibiotics when you don't need to. I think that happens quite often but it's certainly not a good thing.

turns.speaker: Anita
turns.text: Enough about me. How are you?

turns.speaker: Ted
turns.text: Well, I had the flu last month and I'm just fully recovered now.

dialogues.title: The Hangover
dialogues.intro: Terry is talking to Sandra about how tired he is.

turns.speaker: Terry
turns.text: I wish I hadn't stayed out so late last night. I feel terrible today.

turns.speaker: Sandra
turns.text: You also drank way too much beer. Do you have a hangover?

turns.speaker: Terry
turns.text: Probably, yeah. What's going on today? Anything?

turns.speaker: Sandra
turns.text: Nothing really. I was going to catch up on some work. Maybe go for a bike ride.

turns.speaker: Terry
turns.text: Okay. I think I'm going to take a nap then.

turns.speaker: Sandra
turns.text: Good plan. Catch some Z's and you'll feel better.

turns.speaker: Terry
turns.text: Wake me up in time for dinner, okay? I don't want to sleep too long because I won't be able to sleep tonight.

turns.speaker: Sandra
turns.text: Sure thing.

dialogues.title: Summer vacation
dialogues.intro: Kev and Terry are talking about their plans.

turns.speaker: Kev
turns.text: What are you doing for summer vacation?

turns.speaker: Terry
turns.text: I'm looking into going camping. I still have to book a site though.

turns.speaker: Kev
turns.text: Where do you want to go?

turns.speaker: Terry
turns.text: To Cultus Lake. It's beautiful there plus there are waterslides for the kids and a pub for me!

turns.speaker: Kev
turns.text: That sounds just about perfect. I hope you can get a site. They book up quickly. I'm going to do a mini stay-cation and do lots of day hikes and stuff like that.

turns.speaker: Terry
turns.text: Sounds nice too. Where do you like to go hiking?

turns.speaker: Kev
turns.text: I got a new book, "Hikes in the Fraser Valley" so Ill check out some of those ones.

dialogues.title: Dusk and Dawn
dialogues.intro: Ted and Tony are talking about fishing.

turns.speaker: Tony
turns.text: What are you up to these days now that you're retired?

turns.speaker: Ted
turns.text: Just doing lots of fishing.

turns.speaker: Tony
turns.text: Oh cool, when do you go?

turns.speaker: Ted
turns.text: Pretty frequently, at least twice a week. I get up before the sun rises and go for a few hours. Then, I take a nap midday and go out again after dinner for a couple of hours.

turns.speaker: Tony
turns.text: Oh yeah, I've heard that dusk and dawn are the best times, right?

turns.speaker: Ted
turns.text: Yeah, definitely. Nothing is biting in the middle of the day.

dialogues.title: What's on TV?
dialogues.intro: Jerry and Linda are talking about what they're watching on Netflix.

turns.speaker: Jerry
turns.text: What are you watching on Netfix these days?

turns.speaker: Lana
turns.text: The Crown. It's so good. Have you seen it?

turns.speaker: Jerry
turns.text: I know everyone is talking about it but I'm just not interested in the Royal family.

turns.speaker: Lana
turns.text: So what are you watching?

turns.speaker: Jerry
turns.text: Well, I love sports stuff so I've been watching Drive to Survive.

turns.speaker: Lana
turns.text: Oh, what's that?

turns.speaker: Jerry
turns.text: It's about the Formula One racing teams. It follows them from race to race and you see the behind-the-scenes stuff. I don't like racing but it's pretty addictive. I binged an entire season in one weekend.

turns.speaker: Lana
turns.text: I'll have to check that out.

dialogues.title: Grab Something to Eat
dialogues.intro: Jenny and Ted are making some plans for the weekend.

turns.speaker: Jenny
turns.text: Ted, let's hang out this weekend! It's been a while.

turns.speaker: Ted
turns.text: I know, right? We haven't hung out in months. I'd love to do something. What do you think?

turns.speaker: Jenny
turns.text: The weather is kind of iffy but what about going for a hike? And then we can grab something to eat after?

turns.speaker: Ted
turns.text: That's great. Let's go to Mount Seymour. I haven't been there in a long time and it'll be a piece of cake even though I'm out of shape! Rain or shine is good for me.

turns.speaker: Jenny
turns.text: Perfect. I can drive. I'll pick you up at 1:00?

turns.speaker: Ted
turns.text: Okay. See you then! I'll bring snacks for us.

turns.speaker: Jenny
turns.text: Perfect.

dialogues.title: Moving
dialogues.intro: Amy is asking Zeke for help with moving.

turns.speaker: Amy
turns.text: Hey Zeke, you have a truck, right? Can you help me move next weekend? I think it'll take about three hours. Is $100 fair?

turns.speaker: Zeke
turns.text: I do have a truck and I can also help you move.

turns.speaker: Amy
turns.text: Great! | appreciate it.

turns.speaker: Zeke
turns.text: But, I don't want your money. That's what friends are for, right?

turns.speaker: Amy
turns.text: Zeke! I know everyone probably wants you to help them because you have a truck, right? It must get annoying.

turns.speaker: Zeke
turns.text: You are the first person I've helped this year. It's all good.

turns.speaker: Amy
turns.text: Okay. Well, we'll get some pizza and beer afterwards. My treat.

turns.speaker: Zeke
turns.text: That sounds great.

dialogues.title: Build In
dialogues.intro: Keith and Jen are talking about what their plans are for the weekend.

turns.speaker: Keith
turns.text: Should we talk about our weekend plans?

turns.speaker: Jen
turns.text: Sure, my main priority is staying up to watch the Oilers and then getting up late the next day. But let's build in some time for cleaning and organizing too. Our house is getting so messy.

turns.speaker: Keith
turns.text: I figured on that. Let's pull out the couch and do a deep clean. And also put together that new coffee table. We've been so lazy.

turns.speaker: Jen
turns.text: Let's do it. And what about food? We have that soup from yesterday we can heat up for a couple of meals but we'll need to pick up groceries.

turns.speaker: Keith
turns.text: Sure thing.

dialogues.title: Pizza for Dinner?
dialogues.intro: Ted is talking to his husband Tony about what to eat for diner.

turns.speaker: Ted
turns.text: Tony, what should we have for dinner?

turns.speaker: Tony
turns.text: Hmm... what do we have in our fridge? Maybe we could have a tofu stir-fry? We have lots of vegetables we need to eat I think. Ill make that homemade sweet & sour sauce that you like.

turns.speaker: Ted
turns.text: That doesn't sound exciting to me. Why don't I pick up a pizza on the way home from work?

turns.speaker: Tony
turns.text: Ted! Didn't we agree to stop spending so much money on take-out? I'll make the stir-fry, you lazy guy!

turns.speaker: Ted
turns.text: Yes, we did agree to stop spending so much money. You can cook me dinner then. If you insist. But let's put pineapple in too. You know how much I love that.

turns.speaker: Tony
turns.text: I'll do it. It's only because I love you so much though.

turns.speaker: Ted
turns.text: I love you too.

dialogues.title: At Breakfast
dialogues.intro: Allen is complaining on the phone to his friend Terry about his son Nate who is a picky eater.

turns.speaker: Terry
turns.text: Allen? Hey, what's up?

turns.speaker: Allen
turns.text: At this very moment, I'm so angry at Nate. He's suddenly decided, at the age of 12, to become the world's pickiest eater.

turns.speaker: Terry
turns.text: What happened?

turns.speaker: Allen
turns.text: Well at breakfast, he decided he wasn't going to eat cereal anymore and that I should cook him eggs, pancakes or waffles every day. And then at lunch, he didn't want the pasta that I made which he usually loves.

turns.speaker: Terry
turns.text: Ohhh...that's frustrating.

turns.speaker: Allen
turns.text: It gets worse. By the time dinner came around, I was already fuming so I asked what he'd like. He said pizza so I made his favourite kind-ham and pineapple. Then he sat down and said that he meant from the pizza shop. Not homemade pizza. I seldom yell but at that point, I told him to go to his room and that he couldn't have any dinner.

turns.speaker: Terry
turns.text: Oh no! How did it end?

turns.speaker: Allen
turns.text: Well, later that evening, he came down and apologized for being so difficult and asked if there was any leftover pizza.

dialogues.title: My fair share
dialogues.intro: Bob and Min-Sun are talking about splitting chores.

turns.speaker: Bob
turns.text: Min-Sun, can I talk to you about something? I'm doing more than my fair share of chores. I do all the grocery shopping and cooking, laundry, and most of the cleaning too.

turns.speaker: Min-Sun
turns.text: I know. You're right. I'm sorry. Ive been so busy at work that when I get home, I just want to relax.

turns.speaker: Bob
turns.text: I'm tired of it though.

turns.speaker: Min-Sun
turns.text: Why don't we make a chart? I think I'd do better if I knew the things I was 100% responsible for. Right now, it's not on my mind. Like every Saturday, I clean the bathrooms. Or, I have to cook dinner on Tuesday and Thursday night.

turns.speaker: Bob
turns.text: Sure, we can do that. Let's see how it goes.

turns.speaker: Min-Sun
turns.text: Thanks for bringing this up. I don't want you to feel like you have to do everything.

dialogues.title: The New House
dialogues.intro: Liz is talking to Cheryl about her new house.

turns.speaker: Liz
turns.text: Didn't you just move? I think I heard you mention that.

turns.speaker: Cheryl
turns.text: Yes, I moved to Coquitlam from Maple Ridge.

turns.speaker: Liz
turns.text: Oh, exciting! Why did you move?

turns.speaker: Cheryl
turns.text: Well, I was tired of commuting so far. I work downtown and Coquilam is around 20 minutes closer.

turns.speaker: Liz
turns.text: For sure. How's everything at the new place?

turns.speaker: Cheryl
turns.text: Well, it's smaller so I've had to downsize. But it's easier having fewer things. I'm starting to embrace simplicity.

turns.speaker: Liz
turns.text: I need more of that in my life! I feel like I'm always cleaning and looking after my things.

turns.speaker: Cheryl
turns.text: Check out that Netflix show with Marie Kondo. She was my guide. Everything you own should bring you joy.

turns.speaker: Liz
turns.text: I'll have a look. I need a new show to watch.

dialogues.title: Getting to school
dialogues.intro: Min-Sun and Bob are talking about how they get to school.

turns.speaker: Min-Sun
turns.text: How are you doing?

turns.speaker: Bob
turns.text: Okay, but I'm so tired.

turns.speaker: Min-Sun
turns.text: Why? A bad sleep?

turns.speaker: Bob
turns.text: No, a short one. I have to commute for two hours each way, so early morning classes are the worst for me. I have to get up at 5:00.

turns.speaker: Min-Sun
turns.text: Where do you live?

turns.speaker: Bob
turns.text: Oh, I live in Pitt Meadows.

turns.speaker: Min-Sun
turns.text: That's terrible.

turns.speaker: Bob
turns.text: I know, but I live with my parents for free. It's not all bad. I am thinking about moving out next year though.

dialogues.title: Let's Clean the House
dialogues.intro: Sandy and Logan are talking about cleaning the house this weekend.

turns.speaker: Sandy
turns.text: So what are we going to do this weekend?

turns.speaker: Logan
turns.text: Our house. It's so disorganized and filthy. We need to clean it up.

turns.speaker: Sandy
turns.text: Really? I don't think it's that bad.

turns.speaker: Logan
turns.text: It's bad. Do you not see all those fuzzy things in the fridge?

turns.speaker: Sandy
turns.text: I have noticed that, yes. But you always take care of that.

turns.speaker: Logan
turns.text: Okay, I will. But what about all those dishes on the counter and the toilets that haven't been scrubbed in weeks?

turns.speaker: Sandy
turns.text: Okay, you're right. Let's do that Saturday morning.

turns.speaker: Logan
turns.text: Sure. Let's do a good job though. I want everything to sparkle.

dialogues.title: Talking about an accident
dialogues.intro: Sammy and Kerry are talking about an accident.

turns.speaker: Sammy
turns.text: Oh Kerry! Are you okay? Why do you have all those bruises?

turns.speaker: Kerry
turns.text: I went over the handlebars while riding my bike.

turns.speaker: Sammy
turns.text: Oh no! You look terrible.

turns.speaker: Kerry
turns.text: Thanks! Haha. I hit my head but no serious damage because I was wearing a helmet. Just a cut on my leg and some scrapes on my hands.

turns.speaker: Sammy
turns.text: Thank god for that. How did you not break any bones?

turns.speaker: Kerry
turns.text: I'm not sure. They did an x-ray of my entire body at the hospital, and I also got a CAT scan of my head. They were worried about bleeding in my brain. Thankfully, nothing besides cuts and bruises.

turns.speaker: Sammy
turns.text: I'm happy to hear that you're okay! It could have been way worse.

dialogues.title: At One Time
dialogues.intro: Patty and Ryan are talking about being a police officer.

turns.speaker: Patty
turns.text: So what did you want to be when you were growing up?

turns.speaker: Ryan
turns.text: Oh, at one time, I wanted to be a police officer but I see now that working the night shift is terrible for your health.

turns.speaker: Patty
turns.text: Not only that, but i think that cops are constantly changing between nights and days.

turns.speaker: Ryan
turns.text: My friend told me that they change shifts weekly and that he sometimes loses track of days.

turns.speaker: Patty
turns.text: For sure, you'd never get a good night's sleep. But, maybe you'd be so exhausted that you could fall asleep in no time. I would never want to do it though!

dialogues.title: Eating Habits
dialogues.intro: Sara and Lucy are talking about bad eating habits.

turns.speaker: Sara
turns.text: Long time, no see. What's up?

turns.speaker: Lucy
turns.text: Oh, not much. Just watching way too much TV and eating junk food. All my activities got cancelled because of Covid.

turns.speaker: Sara
turns.text: Same here. I'm so bored. I just eat chips and popcorn and watch movies almost every night.

turns.speaker: Lucy
turns.text: I totally get that. You know what. We should start going for walks once or twice a week at night. What do you think?

turns.speaker: Sara
turns.text: That's the best idea. I need to get out of the house more and get some exercise.

turns.speaker: Lucy
turns.text: Okay, let's start tomorrow night. I'll come to your house around 7:30. Would that work?

turns.speaker: Sara
turns.text: Sure, sounds good.

turns.speaker: Team leader
turns.text: I wanted to give you an update. We're a bit down on our luck because of Covid-19 and are struggling to make ends meet. On your end, please put a lid on expenses. From the management side of things, we're going to change suppliers and stop paying too much for raw materials. We all have to tighten our belts around here because I have no card up my sleeve. We either do this or well go bankrupt. That's it for the pep talk! Any questions?

turns.speaker: Employee
turns.text: Okay, boss. That's crystal clear. My team will double down on our sales efforts and pay close attention to expenses.

dialogues.title: I'm so Tired
dialogues.intro: Terry is talking to Sandra about how tired he is.

turns.speaker: Terry
turns.text: I wish I hadn't stayed out so late last night. I feel terrible today.

turns.speaker: Sandra
turns.text: You also drank way too much beer. Do you have a hangover?

turns.speaker: Terry
turns.text: Probably, yeah. What's going on today? Anything?

turns.speaker: Sandra
turns.text: Nothing really. I was going to catch up on some work. Maybe go for a bike ride.

turns.speaker: Terry
turns.text: Okay. I think I'm going to take a nap then.

turns.speaker: Sandra
turns.text: Good plan. Catch some Z's and you'll feel better.

turns.speaker: Terry
turns.text: Wake me up in time for dinner, okay? I don't want to sleep too long because I won't be able to sleep tonight.

turns.speaker: Sandra
turns.text: Sure thing.

dialogues.title: Not feeling great
dialogues.intro: Emma is talking to Mabel (her grandmother) on the phone about her health problems.

turns.speaker: Emma
turns.text: Hi Grandma, how are you feeling today?

turns.speaker: Mabel
turns.text: Honestly, not great. My legs hurt so much today. I went for a walk yesterday, but I think I went for too long.

turns.speaker: Emma
turns.text: Oh no. How far did you go?

turns.speaker: Mabel
turns.text: Well, to the mall and back.

turns.speaker: Emma
turns.text: Grandma! That's too far. Isn't it like 5 km one way? Call me if you need to go there. I can take you.

turns.speaker: Mabel
turns.text: Okay, I will next time, but I don't like to bother anyone. And you know that I don't like to take the bus.

turns.speaker: Emma
turns.text: It's no problem at all. I'd love to help you. You shouldn't walk so far. Please call me!

dialogues.title: It's Hot in Here
dialogues.intro: Brenda and Ho-Hyun are talking about how hot it is in their house.

turns.speaker: Brenda
turns.text: This heat wave is crazy. It's boiling in here.

turns.speaker: Ho-Hyun
turns.text: For real. It must be at least 30 degrees in our bedroom.

turns.speaker: Brenda
turns.text: Why don't we get air conditioning? I know it's expensive but it'll be worth it

turns.speaker: Ho-Hyun
turns.text: It'll be more than a thousand bucks. And we'd only use it for 4-5 days a year. It's not worth it.

turns.speaker: Brenda
turns.text: I know you're right. I'm just worried that we'll get heatstroke in our own house!

turns.speaker: Ho-Hyun
turns.text: You're not going to get heatstroke. Trust me. Why don't we go to the store and buy another fan? That way, we can each have one pointing at us at all times.

turns.speaker: Brenda
turns.text: Sure, and let's get some ice cream and refreshing drinks too.

turns.speaker: Ho-Hyun
turns.text: Okay, let's go. And how about going to the movie theater first and catching a flick? It's always nice and cool in there.

dialogues.title: At the coffee shop
dialogues.intro: Cameron and Marnie are talking about what they're going to order.

turns.speaker: Cameron
turns.text: I never go to coffee shops! What do you usually get here?

turns.speaker: Marnie
turns.text: I usually get a latte. They make a nice one here.

turns.speaker: Cameron
turns.text: Okay, I'll get that with oat milk. I'm kind of hungry too. I think I'll get something to eat too.

turns.speaker: Marnie
turns.text: They have some nice sandwiches and salad. I usually get the pesto, tomato and mozzarella sandwich or the quinoa salad.

turns.speaker: Cameron
turns.text: Amazing. I'll take your recommendation on that one too and go for the salad. Thanks for your help!

turns.speaker: Marnie
turns.text: No problem at all! I spend too much money here.

dialogues.title: In the 40s
dialogues.intro: Harry is talking to his grandmother about the past.

turns.speaker: Harry
turns.text: So what was life like in the past?

turns.speaker: Dianne
turns.text: Well, I grow up in the 40s. It was an interesting time. World War 2 has just ended and the economy was booming as all the men returned home. It was the defining moment of the 20th century in my opinion.

turns.speaker: Harry
turns.text: Oh wow. That does sound like an interesting time. I personally can't imagine life without the Internet.

turns.speaker: Dianne
turns.text: I know it seems crazy now, right? You kids born in the 21s century have just grown up with it. I wonder what life will be like in 20 years' time?

turns.speaker: Harry
turns.text: That's way off in the future. Who knows! Maybe flying cars?

turns.speaker: Dianne
turns.text: We'll see if I live long enough to see it!

dialogues.title: Save the Environment
dialogues.intro: Tammy is annoyed at Doug for not recycling.

turns.speaker: Tammy
turns.text: Doug. I took out the trash this morning and I saw all kinds of things that can be recycled

turns.speaker: Doug
turns.text: Like what?

turns.speaker: Tammy
turns.text: Well, pickle jars, soda cans, tin cans, flyers. Almost everything in the trash could have been recycled.

turns.speaker: Doug
turns.text: Well, how do you know it was me?

turns.speaker: Tammy
turns.text: You're the only person who lives here besides me. And I always recycle. I care about the environment.

turns.speaker: Doug
turns.text: Are you saying that I don't care about it?

turns.speaker: Tammy
turns.text: Well...I think you could do more.

turns.speaker: Doug
turns.text: Hmmm. I don't know about that.

dialogues.title: Ran Into You
dialogues.intro: Carrie and Tim bumped into each other at the grocery store.

turns.speaker: Tim
turns.text: Carrie!

turns.speaker: Carrie
turns.text: Wow, it's been a while, right? Maybe a year?

turns.speaker: Tim
turns.text: Yeah, I think it was around Christmas last year that I ran into you at the mall. I was doing my last-minute shopping.

turns.speaker: Carrie
turns.text: That's right. What's up with you?

turns.speaker: Tim
turns.text: Just busy at work. Not much besides that. How about you?

turns.speaker: Carrie
turns.text: I got a new dog and we've been having so much fun with him.

turns.speaker: Tim
turns.text: Nice! Anyway, nice to see you again! I gotta run pick up Tony from soccer pretty soon.

turns.speaker: Carrie
turns.text: For sure. Let's catch up over coffee soon.

dialogues.title: The typhoon
dialogues.intro: Toni and Marnie are talking about what they saw on the news last night.

turns.speaker: Toni
turns.text: Did you hear about the big typhoon that hit Japan last night?

turns.speaker: Marnie
turns.text: So crazy, right? I heard the winds were almost 300 km/h.

turns.speaker: Toni
turns.text: I hope everyone was prepared for it.

turns.speaker: Marnie
turns.text: I think they get typhoons there every year. They must know what to do, right?

turns.speaker: Toni
turns.text: I'm sure they were prepared for it. I haven't heard that anyone has died yet.

turns.speaker: Marnie
turns.text: I hope it turns out okay for everyone.

turns.speaker: Toni
turns.text: Me too. I hate to see stuff like that on the news.

dialogues.title: Pet Peeves
dialogues.intro: Bo-Hyun and Amir are talking about their pet peeves.

turns.speaker: Bo-Hyun
turns.text: So do you have any pet peeves?

turns.speaker: Amir
turns.text: So many. Where to start. My biggest one is slow walkers. And then getting stuck behind them on a sidewalk. What's one of yours?

turns.speaker: Bo-Hyun
turns.text: Oh yeah, that's annoying for sure. Hmm...I hate TV commercials. So much. That's why I only watch Netlix these days. Or, lil pay for live streaming for sports.

turns.speaker: Amir
turns.text: I know, right? Who wants to sit through that?

turns.speaker: Bo-Hyun
turns.text: Every time I see an ad for ice cream or fast food, I want to go out and buy it ifs not easy to resist.

turns.speaker: Amir
turns.text: I feel your pain, my friend.

dialogues.title: The Superbowl
dialogues.intro: Joni and Sid are talking about the Superbow!

turns.speaker: Joni
turns.text: Did you see the big game last night?

turns.speaker: Sid
turns.text: Of course! Who didn't?

turns.speaker: Joni
turns.text: What did you think?

turns.speaker: Sid
turns.text: To be honest, I thought the game was kind of boring. The real star was the half-time show. I couldn't believe how well done it was. I even watched it again on YouTube this morning.

turns.speaker: Joni
turns.text: I have to admit, I don't like Shakira, so I skipped the show! I made al kinds of snacks during halftime instead. Chicken wings, pizza, popcorn, all the things.

turns.speaker: Sid
turns.text: I need to come to your house next year. The snacks are the only reason I go to Superbowl parties.

dialogues.title: Booked Off
dialogues.intro: Kevin and Tony are talking about their plans.

turns.speaker: Kevin
turns.text: What are you doing for summer vacation?

turns.speaker: Tony
turns.text: Well, I just booked off some time to go camping. I need to chill out. I've been burning the candle at both ends for months now.

turns.speaker: Kevin
turns.text: I know. You work like a dog. Where are you headed to?

turns.speaker: Tony
turns.text: To Cultus Lake. It's beautiful there plus there are waterslides for the kids and a pub for me!

turns.speaker: Kevin
turns.text: That sounds just about perfect. I'm going to do a mini staycation and do lots of day hikes and stuff like that.

turns.speaker: Tony
turns.text: Sounds nice too. Where do you like hiking?

turns.speaker: Kevin
turns.text: I'm just getting into it now. I bought a book though so I'll do some stuff from there.

dialogues.title: At the Movie Theater
dialogues.intro: Matt is buying some tickets for a movie.

turns.speaker: Ticket Agent
turns.text: Hi, what would you like to see?

turns.speaker: Matt
turns.text: Batman.

turns.speaker: Ticket Agent
turns.text: Sure, the next showing is at 7:00. Is that good?

turns.speaker: Matt
turns.text: Yes, please.

turns.speaker: Ticket Agent
turns.text: For how many people?

turns.speaker: Matt
turns.text: Four.

turns.speaker: Ticket Agent
turns.text: Okay, and any preference of where to sit?

turns.speaker: Matt
turns.text: Somewhere near the back please, in the middle. Oh, and my wife likes the aisle seat.

turns.speaker: Ticket Agent
turns.text: Sure, we have some seats available.

turns.speaker: Matt
turns.text: I'd like to get some snack combos. Can I pay for that here?

turns.speaker: Ticket Agent
turns.text: No, you can order that at the concession.

turns.speaker: Matt
turns.text: Sure.

turns.speaker: Ticket Agent
turns.text: Okay, here are your tickets. You're in theater 6 at 7:00.

dialogues.title: Talking About an Accident
dialogues.intro: Sam and Kerry are talking about an accident.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Oh Kerry! What happened?

turns.speaker: Kerry
turns.text: I hit a rock while riding my bike and took a tumble over the handlebars.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Oh no! It looks bad

turns.speaker: Kerry
turns.text: I got rushed to ER. I hit my head pretty hard but no serious damage because I was wearing a helmet. Just a cut on my leg and some scrapes on my hands.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Thank God for that. How did you not break any bones? You must have nine lives.

turns.speaker: Kerry
turns.text: I'm not sure. It's a small miracle. They did an x-ray of my entire body to check and I also got a CAT scan of my head which was interesting. They were worried about bleeding in my brain.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: I'm happy to hear that you're okay! You'll be back to your adventure in no time at all.

dialogues.title: How was Italy?
dialogues.intro: Sara and Lucy are talking about holidays.

turns.speaker: Sara
turns.text: Didn't you just get back from Italy? How was it?

turns.speaker: Lucy
turns.text: So amazing. The food! It was the best vacation ever.

turns.speaker: Sara
turns.text: What did you like so much besides the food?

turns.speaker: Lucy
turns.text: It was so beautiful. And the food. I'll mention that again. I ate my way from place to place. Actually, there wasn't anything I didn't like about it.

turns.speaker: Sara
turns.text: Fun! I'm happy that you had such a great time. I need a vacation!

turns.speaker: Lucy
turns.text: You definitely do. You've been working too hard lately.

dialogues.title: Managers Talking About Employees
dialogues.intro: Jeremiah and Katelyn are talking about employees taking long lunches.

turns.speaker: Jeremiah
turns.text: Have you noticed that everyone is taking long lunches? They're pushing the boundaries for sure.

turns.speaker: Katelyn
turns.text: I have actually. I think we need to clamp down on it before it cuts into our bottom line. We'll have to be careful though. It's a catch-22 because we expect them to work OT regularly.

turns.speaker: Jeremiah
turns.text: It's true, but they get paid a pretty penny for that I think we should stand our ground. Let's try a friendly reminder to see if we get the results we want.

turns.speaker: Katelyn
turns.text: Good idea. We're on the same wavelength here.

dialogues.title: Up to Date
dialogues.intro: Min-Guy is asking Shuo for some advice about getting a new phone.

turns.speaker: Min-Gyu
turns.text: Hey Shuo, you're up to date on the latest technology. I'm thinking about getting a new phone. Can you lend me a hand?

turns.speaker: Shuo
turns.text: Ah, what do you have now?

turns.speaker: Min-Gyu
turns.text: An iPhone but it's old and slow now. I want something bigger and better.

turns.speaker: Shuo
turns.text: Are you happy with the iPhone or are you considering switching?

turns.speaker: Min-Gyu
turns.text: Honestly, I'm ambivalent. What do you think?

turns.speaker: Shuo
turns.text: Well, the Samsung phones are nice and have more bang for the buck. You pay a premium for Apple stuff.

turns.speaker: Min-Gyu
turns.text: I'm open to switching. Do you have a model recommendation?

turns.speaker: Shuo
turns.text: Let me look into it a bit and I'll text you later, okay?

dialogues.title: Talking About Retirement
dialogues.intro: Neil and Bob are talking about retirement.

turns.speaker: Neil
turns.text: I can't hack it anymore. I'm so burnt out.

turns.speaker: Bob
turns.text: I hear ya. Climbing the corporate ladder takes a lot out of someone. Why not cash In your chips and retire? You'll be well off with that pension plan.

turns.speaker: Neil
turns.text: I can't put my finger on it but I don't want to for some reason. Maybe I'm scared of what will come next?

turns.speaker: Bob
turns.text: I understand that. But don't work yourself to death, okay? Maybe you could have your cake and eat it too. Retire, and then do some consulting?
